name: Garden Thyme
description: A subtle, earthy herb that stands up to long cooking times in stews, soups, and roasts.
uses: Bouquet garni in soups and stews
Flavoring grilled chicken and roast vegetables
Thymol extraction for natural throat soothe
Thyme tea and syrup are long-standing remedies for coughs and sore throats
Used in natural mouthwashes and gargles for its antiseptic action
Steam inhalation traditionally used to loosen chest congestion
benefits: Thymol, its main compound, has antibacterial and antifungal properties
Good source of vitamin C and vitamin A
Antioxidants help protect cells from everyday damage
medicinal.caution: Thyme essential oil is very strong and must be diluted. Culinary and tea amounts are considered safe for most people.

taste: Earthy and warm, with subtle lemon and mint notes.
sideEffects: Thyme essential oil is very strong and can irritate the skin and mouth
Large medicinal amounts may upset the stomach
Rarely causes allergic reactions in people sensitive to mint-family plants

safety.allergy: Thyme is a mint-family plant, so people who react to oregano, mint or lavender may react to it. Stop using it if you get a rash or swelling.
safety.pregnancy: Normal cooking amounts are considered safe. Avoid medicinal doses and the oil unless a doctor agrees.
safety.pets: Thyme is generally regarded as safe for cats and dogs in small amounts, but the essential oil is not.
safety.medications: Thyme in food amounts is not known to cause problems, but ask your doctor about concentrated extracts if you take blood thinners.

temperature: Very hardy: common thyme survives winter cold of about -20 °C and also copes with hot, dry summers. It grows best at about 15-30 °C.
harvest: Snip stems just above a pair of leaves at any time, but the flavor is best just before the plant flowers. Cut little and often, and leave the woody base to regrow.
storage: Keep fresh sprigs in a damp paper towel in the fridge for about two weeks. Thyme dries extremely well and keeps its flavor, and it can also be frozen on the stem.
dailyLife: Add whole sprigs to soups, stews and roasts
Make honey-sweetened thyme tea for a scratchy throat
Rub on chicken or fish before cooking
Mix into butter or olive oil
tips: Plant it in gritty, free-draining soil
Trim after flowering so it stays compact
Let it spill over a wall or path, it likes to be stepped on lightly

origin.region: Southern Europe and the Mediterranean (Greece, Italy and Spain)
origin.details: Thyme grows wild on the dry hills of southern Europe. The ancient Greeks burned it as incense and used it for courage and cleansing.
